newsitem.title: CHINA: Number of China industrial workers falls in H1.
newsitem.headline: Number of China industrial workers falls in H1.

text.p: The number of workers employed in China's industrial sector fell by a year-on-year 186,000 in the first half of 1997 to 146.7 million, officials said on Wednesday.
Town and village industrial enterprises shed about 1.2 million workers in the first half, with employees in the sector totalling 28.77 million, said one official with the Ministry of Labour.
"The drop was partly caused by enterprises laying off more and more workers," the official said.
The number of industrial workers in the state sector rose by 84,000 in the half compared to the year-ago period, hitting 108.5 million, she said.
Those in solely foreign-owned and foreign joint ventures rose by 920,000 to 9.45 million in the period, she said.
China has not released unemployment figures for the first half but the official urban jobless rate was about 3.1 percent at the end of March, hitting 5.63 million, she said.
That was a rise of 6.3 percent from the same period the year before, she said.
China's official unemployment figures consist only of urban unemployed who have registered with the government to help them find work.
Officials have said if the 7.5 million redundant employees of state enterprises that have stopped or slashed production were included, the urban unemployment rate would rise to about 4.5 percent.
